questions.q: Hyaline cartilage is found in all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: IV discs are fibrocartilage (shock absorbers). Hyaline cartilage is in trachea, articular surfaces, nose, larynx, costal cartilage.

questions.q: Elastic cartilage is found in:
questions.exp: Elastic cartilage (with elastin fibres) is found in the external ear (pinna), epiglottis, and Eustachian tube.

questions.q: Fibrocartilage is found in:
questions.exp: Fibrocartilage (Type I collagen-rich) is found in IV discs, pubic symphysis, menisci — shock absorbers.

questions.q: Compact bone is mainly found in:
questions.exp: Compact (cortical) bone forms the diaphysis (shaft) of long bones, providing strength.
optExp: Marrow cavity contains marrow, not compact bone.
Flat bones have spongy interior between compact layers.

questions.q: Spongy (trabecular) bone is found in:
opts: Found primarily in the epiphysis and metaphysis
questions.exp: Spongy bone (with trabeculae) is in the epiphyses of long bones and in flat bones, containing red marrow.

questions.q: Intramembranous ossification is responsible for forming:
questions.exp: Intramembranous ossification forms flat bones from mesenchymal cells directly (e.g. skull vault, mandible, clavicle). Closes fontanelles by ~age 2.

questions.q: Endochondral ossification involves:
opts: Ossification directly from mesenchyme without a cartilage template
Ossification of a pre-existing cartilage model
Calcification of fibrous tendons and ligaments
Bone formation that occurs only in adult life
Formation of dental tissues and tooth enamel
questions.exp: Endochondral ossification produces long bones (and pelvis, ribs, vertebrae) by replacing a cartilage model with bone.
optExp: Begins in utero, continues to puberty.

questions.q: Which cell breaks down bone tissue?
questions.exp: Osteoclasts are large multinucleated cells (from monocyte lineage) that resorb bone via H⁺ and proteases.
optExp: Fibroblasts make collagen in connective tissue.

questions.q: Osteocytes reside in:
opts: Within lacunae in the bone matrix
questions.exp: Osteocytes are osteoblasts that became trapped in lacunae of the mineralised bone matrix, communicating via canaliculi.
optExp: Haversian canals contain vessels and nerves.

questions.q: Chondrocytes are housed within:
opts: Within lacunae in the cartilage matrix
questions.exp: Chondrocytes sit in lacunae within the cartilage matrix; cartilage is avascular and relies on diffusion.

questions.q: The growth plate (epiphyseal plate) zones from epiphysis to diaphysis include:
opts: Calcification zone → hypertrophic zone → proliferation zone → resting zone
Resting zone → proliferation zone → hypertrophic zone → calcification zone
Hypertrophic zone → resting zone → calcification zone → proliferation zone
Proliferation zone → resting zone → calcification zone → hypertrophic zone
Resting zone → calcification zone → proliferation zone → hypertrophic zone
questions.exp: Mnemonic 'Really Poor Habits Cause Osteoporosis': Resting (Reserved) → Proliferation → Hypertrophic → Calcification.

questions.q: In osteogenesis imperfecta, the defective protein is:
questions.exp: OI is caused by mutations in COL1A1/COL1A2 (Type I collagen), causing brittle bones, blue sclerae, hearing loss.

questions.q: Tendons and ligaments are composed of:
questions.exp: Tendons/ligaments are dense regular CT — collagen fibres aligned in parallel to resist tension along one direction.

questions.q: The periosteum and perichondrium are examples of:
questions.exp: Dense irregular CT has interwoven collagen bundles, providing strength in multiple directions (dermis, periosteum, perichondrium).

questions.q: Reticular fibres are predominantly found in:
questions.exp: Reticular fibres (Type III collagen) form the stroma of lymph nodes, spleen, and bone marrow.

questions.q: Which connective tissue cell synthesises collagen and ECM?
questions.exp: Fibroblasts are the main producers of collagen, elastin, and ECM ground substance in connective tissue.

questions.q: Adipose tissue's main function is:
questions.exp: White adipose tissue stores energy as triglycerides; brown adipose generates heat.

questions.q: Elastic fibres are most abundant in:
questions.exp: Large elastic arteries (aorta) and lung tissue contain abundant elastin, allowing recoil.
optExp: Hyaline cartilage uses Type II collagen.

questions.q: Skeletal muscle fibres are:
opts: Short cells with a single nucleus
questions.exp: Skeletal muscle: long, cylindrical, multinucleated (peripheral nuclei), striated, voluntary.

questions.q: Cardiac muscle is best identified by:
opts: Multiple nuclei located at the periphery of cells
Lack of visible striations under the microscope
questions.exp: Cardiac myocytes are branched, striated, with 1-2 central nuclei and intercalated discs containing gap junctions.
optExp: Skeletal is uninucleated... wait, skeletal is multinucleated; cardiac has 1-2 central nuclei.

questions.q: Smooth muscle differs from skeletal because:
opts: It has a branched cell structure
questions.exp: Smooth muscle cells are spindle-shaped, non-striated, with a single central nucleus, involuntary control.

questions.q: Intercalated discs are unique to:
questions.exp: Intercalated discs are unique to cardiac muscle, containing desmosomes and gap junctions for electrical and mechanical coupling.
optExp: Smooth muscle uses gap junctions but no intercalated discs.

questions.q: Osteoid is:
questions.exp: Osteoid is the protein-rich, unmineralised matrix laid down by osteoblasts; calcium phosphate later mineralises it to form bone.
optExp: Not a biological term in this context.

questions.q: The Haversian system (osteon) contains:
questions.exp: Each osteon has a Haversian canal (vessels/nerves) surrounded by concentric lamellae, with osteocytes in lacunae linked by canaliculi.

questions.q: Mast cells contain granules of:
questions.exp: Mast cells store histamine, heparin, tryptase — released on IgE crosslinking in allergy/anaphylaxis.

questions.q: Striations in muscle are due to:
opts: Alternating A and I bands with thick and thin filaments
questions.exp: The repeating sarcomere structure with overlapping actin/myosin produces alternating dark (A) and light (I) bands visible as striations.

questions.q: Cartilage receives nutrients via:
questions.exp: Cartilage is avascular and aneural; chondrocytes rely on diffusion through the matrix from the perichondrium.
optExp: Synovial fluid plays a role in joints but main mechanism is diffusion.

questions.q: Cardiac muscle nuclei are typically:
opts: Multiple nuclei arranged at the periphery of the cell
One to two nuclei located centrally within the cell
Completely absent from cardiac muscle cells
Many nuclei distributed randomly throughout the cytoplasm
Nuclei embedded exclusively within the intercalated discs
questions.exp: Cardiac myocytes have 1-2 centrally located nuclei. Skeletal muscle has many peripheral nuclei.
